newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Taylor names new CEO as profits soar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Taylor names new CEO as profits soar.

text.p: Taylor Woodrow Plc named a new chief executive from outside the company on Tuesday after reporting a 45 percent hike in pretax profits, with the housing unit as the star performer.

The group took the rare decision to not draw on its own ranks to fill the post of chief executive when it picked John Castle, formerly of Marley Plc and Textron Inc of the U.S., to succeed Tony Palmer who is retiring after 43 years.
Chairman Colin Parsons said Castle would take over in two months at a time when the outlook for "steady growth" was encouraging.
He added that his international experience would be useful in taking the construction to housing and property group forward.
Pretax profits for 1996 were 66.8 million pounds ($108 million), the top end of market forecasts, with sales rising to 1.19 billion from 1.15 billion pounds.
The yearly dividend was 3.75 pence per share, up from three pence. Taylor Woodrow's shares remained steady after the news, down one pence at 182.
"Taylor Woodrow is now firmly on track...The group has moved forward positively in 1996 in all its inter-related activities," Parson said.
The internationally-spread housing division was the star performer of the results, with profits up 40 percent to 32.8 million pounds.
Taylor Woodrow said this would be the "cornerstone of future growth."
But one concerns for the housing division in the year ahead is land price inflation in the British market as housebuilders scramble for land reserves to build property, chasing up prices in turn.

Echoing others in the sector, Parsons told Reuters: "Land prices in the UK are high. It is very difficult," warning it would become a big problem unless house prices rose to reflect underlying land inflation in the near future.
Greenham Trading, the wholesale merchant business enjoyed steady growth and the other key feature was construction which moved into a tiny profit after heavy losses last year.
Parsons said the group was now ready to move ahead with acquisitions and was willing to gear up from its current debt-to-equity ratio of 11 percent to 30-40 percent to fund deals.
Interest in acquisitions within housing and property development were cited, but Greenham Trading will be grown organically, said the chairman. ($ = 0.618 British Pounds)
